learning_outcomes.text: Use graphical representation techniques, both by traditional methods of metric geometry and descriptive geometry and by computer-aided design applications, in three-dimensional engineering design.

Recognize and understand graphical representation techniques, both by traditional methods of metric geometry and descriptive geometry and by computer-aided design applications, that are applied in three-dimensional engineering design.
Ability to manage NTIC-based environments and their emerging technologies.
Ability to perform laboratory assemblies and experiments.
To project in the field of industrial technical engineering.
To develop projects in the field of industrial technical engineering.
Adapt the organization of content and the use of language, verbal and non-verbal, to argue in diverse situations or before diverse audiences.
Develop measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, task plans and other works typical of the field of technical engineering.
Recognize and understand the legislation necessary for the exercise of the profession of industrial technical engineer.
Show the advantages and opportunities of different solutions to the same problem in a critical and constructive way.
Correctly use, when pertinent, specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Apply the appropriate legislation to the exercise of the industrial technical engineer profession.

syllabus_topics: Representation of Bodies. Standardized Views. Sketching.
assessment_rules: The final grade is composed of Coursework (8%), Other forms of evaluation (7%), Mixed tests (75%), and Continuous assessment (10%). The Mixed tests component includes two exams, Exam 1 (20%) and Exam 2 (55%), held between weeks 6-10 and 15-18 respectively. Evaluation criteria for coursework and other forms of evaluation include clarity, expository correctness, and presentation sequencing. No minimum marks or resit arrangements are specified.
